el-salvador/san-salvador-centro.name: San Salvador historic centre
el-salvador/san-salvador-centro.description: The cathedral, National Palace and Teatro Nacional in the capital.
el-salvador/san-salvador-centro.details: The centre has the Metropolitan Cathedral, which holds the tomb of Archbishop Romero, the National Palace and the Teatro Nacional. Go in daylight and stay in the main plazas. The Museum of Anthropology (MUNA) and the Monument to the Divine Saviour are nearby.

el-salvador/joya-de-ceren.name: Joya de Ceren and Tazumal
el-salvador/joya-de-ceren.description: A buried Maya farming village preserved by volcanic ash, often called the Pompeii of the Americas.
el-salvador/joya-de-ceren.details: Joya de Ceren was buried by the eruption of the Loma Caldera volcano about 1,400 years ago, preserving houses and tools. The nearby Tazumal ruins at Chalchuapa are a larger Maya site. Both are UNESCO-related sites and make a half-day on the way to Santa Ana.

el-salvador/santa-ana-volcano.name: Santa Ana volcano and Lake Coatepeque
el-salvador/santa-ana-volcano.description: A dawn hike to a turquoise crater lake on the highest volcano in the country, and a nearby caldera lake.
el-salvador/santa-ana-volcano.details: The Ilamatepec trail climbs about 2,300 metres to a crater with a bright green lake and steam vents. Hikes require an armed police escort and start at about 11am. The nearby Coatepeque caldera lake is good for swimming and kayaking.

el-salvador/santa-ana-city.name: Santa Ana city and Metapan
el-salvador/santa-ana-city.description: A grand neoclassical city centre with a Gothic cathedral and a theatre.
el-salvador/santa-ana-city.details: Santa Ana has a neo-Gothic cathedral on the main plaza, the Teatro de Santa Ana and a pleasant evening atmosphere. It is a good base for volcanoes, coffee tours and the Ruta de las Flores to the south.

el-salvador/ruta-de-las-flores.name: Ruta de las Flores
el-salvador/ruta-de-las-flores.description: A scenic route through coffee villages with food festivals, murals and waterfalls.
el-salvador/ruta-de-las-flores.details: The Route of Flowers links Nahuizalco, Juayua, Apaneca, Ataco and Ahuachapan. The Juayua food festival runs on weekends, serving local dishes on the main street. Ataco is known for its murals, and coffee farms offer tours. Flowers bloom between November and February.

el-salvador/siete-cascadas.name: Los Chorros and the Seven Waterfalls
el-salvador/siete-cascadas.description: Short hikes to waterfalls and pools in the cloud forest near Juayua.
el-salvador/siete-cascadas.details: The Siete Cascadas trail near Juayua has seven waterfalls and swimming pools. It is a short half-day with a local guide. Wear water shoes, and expect to get wet. Nearby is the Los Chorros park with pools.

el-salvador/el-tunco-surf.name: El Tunco and Pacific surf
el-salvador/el-tunco-surf.description: A surf town with black sand beaches, sunsets and a lively evening scene.
el-salvador/el-tunco-surf.details: El Tunco is the centre of surfing in El Salvador, with waves for all levels and lessons on the beach. Sunsets are famous, and bars and restaurants sit along the main street. El Zonte nearby is a Bitcoin beach town. Beware of strong currents.

el-salvador/suchitoto.name: Suchitoto colonial town
el-salvador/suchitoto.description: A cobbled colonial town on a hill above a reservoir, a centre for arts and culture.
el-salvador/suchitoto.details: Suchitoto has cobbled streets, galleries and indigo workshops. The Cerron Grande reservoir offers boat trips, and waterfalls such as Los Tercios are close. It is about 1.5 hours north of San Salvador.
